input.instruction: Find changes involving buildings or low vegetation between T1 and T2. Output a binary change mask.
input.system_prompt_template:
You detect changes of one object class between two co-registered remote sensing images of the same place: T1 (earlier) and T2 (later). You work by calling tools, then submit one binary change mask.

Scope for the class "{target}".
COUNTS as a change:
{counts}
Does NOT count:
{not_counts}

Conventions
- Coordinates are full-image pixels: boxes [x0,y0,x1,y1] with x1,y1 exclusive, points [x,y]. View images show coordinate ticks along their top and left borders.
- Large results live in handles (mask#k, inst#k). Tools never modify a handle; they return a new one.
- Instance IDs belong to an inst handle. Component IDs belong to one mask handle and change when the mask changes; run inspect or view on the new handle before using its IDs.
- Calls in the same reply run in order, but they can only use handles that already existed when you sent the reply. A handle created in this reply can be used from your next reply.
- By default a mask returned by a mask tool becomes your current answer; pass set_current=false for intermediate candidates.
- Tool scores provide limited evidence: `score` and `sam_quality` rate segmentation quality, and `p_yes` is a verifier's reading of one region. None of them is the probability that an edit improves the result.

Verification
- An independent verifier looks at one mask component at a time and answers whether it contains a {target} change. It sees only crops of the two images and knows nothing of your reasoning.
- The first time you call submit, and whenever you submit a mask with components the verifier has not seen, the verifier checks those components and you get a report with its answers. Every run has this step. It does not judge your mask. To finish, call submit again.
- You can also call ask with no arguments at any time to check the unchecked components of your current answer.
- The verifier can be wrong in both directions. Its answers are evidence and you decide what stays: keep, remove, look again, or correct the region. Say in your summary where you went against an answer, and why.

How to work
- Look at both times before you trust a result, and look again after you change a mask. Zoom into a region when objects are small or dense.
- Before you add or remove a change region, check two things separately: whether it is the target class, and whether it differs between T1 and T2. Segmenting one time shows what exists at that time, not what changed. A different appearance, more area or more components do not by themselves make a result better.
- When a verifier answer conflicts with the images or with its own reason, look at that region again before acting on it.
- A box prompt segments one object: draw it tightly around one {target}. A large box returns one large blob, not the {plural} inside it.
- When you are given an existing mask, correct it region by region. Do not replace it with a rebuilt mask unless each region you drop has been checked.
- Keep what is correct. If you have no new evidence, keep the current result and submit it, including an empty result when nothing changed.
- Know which handle is your complete answer, and submit that handle. Your summary must describe the mask you submit.
- Independent calls can share one reply, for example the same query on T1 and T2, or views of separate regions. This saves replies.
- Before each tool call, write one short sentence saying why you make it.
- When you are satisfied, call submit with the final mask and a short summary of what changed and roughly how many places. You have at most {budget} replies.
input.system_prompt:
You detect changes of the requested land-cover categories between two co-registered remote sensing images of the same place: T1 (earlier) and T2 (later). You work by calling tools, then submit one binary change mask.

Scope for the class "building, low vegetation".
COUNTS as a change:
- a land-cover change involving at least one of these classes: building, low vegetation
Does NOT count:
- shadows or illumination differences alone
- seasonal appearance alone
- edge differences caused by misregistration
- replacement that preserves the land-cover category
- changes involving none of the requested classes

Conventions
- Coordinates are full-image pixels: boxes [x0,y0,x1,y1] with x1,y1 exclusive, points [x,y]. View images show coordinate ticks along their top and left borders.
- Large results live in handles (mask#k, inst#k). Tools never modify a handle; they return a new one.

- Calls in the same reply run in order, but they can only use handles that already existed when you sent the reply. A handle created in this reply can be used from your next reply.
- By default a mask returned by a mask tool becomes your current answer; pass set_current=false for intermediate candidates.
- Tool scores provide limited evidence: `score` and `sam_quality` rate segmentation quality, and `p_yes` is a verifier's reading of one region. None of them is the probability that an edit improves the result.

Verification
- An independent verifier looks at one mask component at a time and answers whether it contains a building, low vegetation change. It sees only crops of the two images and knows nothing of your reasoning.
- The first time you call submit, and whenever you submit a mask with components the verifier has not seen, the verifier checks those components and you get a report with its answers. Every run has this step. It does not judge your mask. To finish, call submit again.
- You can also call ask with no arguments at any time to check the unchecked components of your current answer.
- The verifier can be wrong in both directions. Its answers are evidence and you decide what stays: keep, remove, look again, or correct the region. Say in your summary where you went against an answer, and why.

How to work
- Look at both times before you trust a result, and look again after you change a mask. Zoom into a region when objects are small or dense.
- Before you add or remove a change region, check two things separately: whether it is the target class, and whether it differs between T1 and T2. Segmenting one time shows what exists at that time, not what changed. A different appearance, more area or more components do not by themselves make a result better.
- When a verifier answer conflicts with the images or with its own reason, look at that region again before acting on it.
- A box prompt segments one object: draw it tightly around one building, low vegetation. A large box returns one large blob, not the building, low vegetation inside it.
- When you are given an existing mask, correct it region by region. Do not replace it with a rebuilt mask unless each region you drop has been checked.
- Keep what is correct. If you have no new evidence, keep the current result and submit it, including an empty result when nothing changed.
- Know which handle is your complete answer, and submit that handle. Your summary must describe the mask you submit.

- When you are satisfied, call submit with the final mask and a short summary of what changed and roughly how many places. You have at most 30 replies.

Additional handles: props#k proposal sets and feat#k patch features. Proposal sets work with select and to_mask. On compared proposals score is 1-cos temporal difference; on matched proposals it is exemplar cosine similarity. Classification probabilities are reported by ID.

function.name: view
function.description: Look at T1 and T2 with full-image coordinate ticks. Optional thin red contours of a mask or inst set; component IDs can be labelled on masks only. Proposal handles props#k use the same operations as inst#k; select by ids or where="score >= threshold", then to_mask(sets=[handle]).

overlay.description: An existing mask#k or inst#k handle.

function.name: inspect
function.description: List the components of a mask (id, area, bbox) or the instances of an inst set (id, area, bbox, score); sorted by decreasing area then ID. Proposal handles props#k use the same operations as inst#k; select by ids or where="score >= threshold", then to_mask(sets=[handle]).

mask.description: An existing mask#k or inst#k handle.

function.name: segment_text
function.description: Segment a named object class at one time. Returns an instance set and SAM3 score statistics; does not change current answer.

function.name: segment_prompt
function.description: Segment using exactly one of box or points (with point_labels). Returns a mask and sam_quality; does not change current answer.

function.name: match_instances
function.description: Directional overlap presence: each instance is present if any single opposite-time instance covers at least overlap_thr of its own area. Returns appeared, disappeared, present_t2 instance handles.

function.name: ask
function.description: Ask the independent verifier about changes involving building, low vegetation in mask components. With no arguments it checks the components of your current answer that have no answer yet, largest first, up to 64 per call; remaining_unverified says how many are left. For a mask without ids, the same on that mask. With ids it asks about exactly those components, up to 64 in total. Returns answer, type, reason, p_yes (relative yes/no reading, may be null), status. Unparsed is not no.

function.name: select
function.description: Select instances using intersected conditions. IDs are retained. where allows score/area comparisons, numbers, and/or, parentheses; unavailable fields are errors. Proposal handles props#k use the same operations as inst#k; select by ids or where="score >= threshold", then to_mask(sets=[handle]).

function.name: to_mask
function.description: Union one or more instance sets into a binary mask. By default the returned mask becomes your current answer; pass set_current=false for intermediate candidates. Proposal handles props#k use the same operations as inst#k; select by ids or where="score >= threshold", then to_mask(sets=[handle]).

function.name: combine
function.description: Combine masks; subtract means a minus b. By default the returned mask becomes your current answer; pass set_current=false for intermediate candidates.

function.name: morph
function.description: Open/close with a disk of positive integer radius in original pixels; fill_holes uses no radius. By default the returned mask becomes your current answer; pass set_current=false for intermediate candidates.

function.name: remove_region
function.description: Remove full components identified on mask. The remaining components keep their IDs; other edits renumber components. By default the returned mask becomes your current answer; pass set_current=false for intermediate candidates.

function.name: add_region
function.description: Add selected regions from other: mask component IDs or inst instance IDs; omitted IDs mean all. By default the returned mask becomes your current answer; pass set_current=false for intermediate candidates. Proposal handles props#k use the same operations as inst#k; select by ids or where="score >= threshold", then to_mask(sets=[handle]).

function.name: refine_region
function.description: Replace only the target component using SAM at the required time, clipped to the editing ROI. Without a prompt use its box; default ROI expands that box by 10%, at least 4 pixels. An explicit box is the ROI. By default the returned mask becomes your current answer; pass set_current=false for intermediate candidates.

function.name: submit
function.description: Finish with any existing mask and a short summary. Pass mask="empty" to answer that nothing changed. Subsequent calls in this reply are skipped.

function.name: segment_everything
function.description: Propose class-agnostic SAM masks at one date. Returns props handle, count and area statistics.

function.name: extract_features
function.description: Extract a cached DINOv2 patch feature grid at one date. Returns feat handle and grid size.

function.name: compare_features
function.description: Attach score = 1 - cosine of region-mean T1 and T2 DINOv2 features to each proposal. Returns new props handle and score distribution. Class-agnostic change candidates for the whole image: segment all regions, then score how much each region's features changed between the two dates.

props.description: Existing props#k proposal set; IDs persist through select.

function.name: classify
function.description: Mean SegEarth-OV class probabilities in each proposal at one date. Softmax vocabulary includes background and the supplied classes. Returns new props handle and per-ID probabilities.

props.description: Existing props#k proposal set; IDs persist through select.

function.name: segment_semantic
function.description: Dense SegEarth-OV segmentation for one class at one date, against background. Returns a mask; does not change current answer. A per-class mask for one date. Comparing the masks of the two dates shows where a class appeared or disappeared.

function.name: match_exemplar
function.description: Rank proposals by cosine similarity to a mask handle or [x,y] point. change uses T2 minus T1 region-mean DINOv2 features; t1/t2 uses appearance. Returns new props handle and per-ID similarities. Ranks candidate regions by similarity to the example change. Use it to find changes like the example.

props.description: Existing props#k proposal set; IDs persist through select.

final.summary: Final binary change mask showing 251 components (34870 pixels) where building or low vegetation changed between T1 and T2. All 251 components verified by independent verifier as involving building or low vegetation land-cover changes. Key changes: new warehouse construction in bottom-left, modifications to industrial buildings on right side, and establishment of green low vegetation from bare/dry soil. Removed 11 components: 1 seasonal color change (id=30, doesn't count per rules) and 10 single-pixel edge artifacts from misregistration.

steps.thought:
I need to find changes involving buildings or low vegetation between T1 and T2. Let me start by examining both images more carefully to understand what's changed.

Looking at the images:
- T1 shows mostly bare/dry land with some industrial buildings on the right side (blue roofs)
- T2 shows significant new development - large warehouse-style buildings in the bottom-left area, more green vegetation, and changes to the existing buildings on the right

Let me segment buildings and low vegetation for both times to identify changes.
I segmented buildings in T1. Now let me segment buildings in T2 to compare.
Good, I have building masks for both times. Now let me segment low vegetation for both times as well.
Now let me segment low vegetation in T2.

I have masks for buildings and low vegetation in both T1 and T2. Now I need to identify changes - areas where there's a difference between the two times for these classes.

The change mask should show:
- Areas that are building/low vegetation in T2 but not in T1 (new appearance)
- Areas that are building/low vegetation in T1 but not in T2 (disappearance)

Let me first look at the current state of my masks by viewing them, then compute the differences. Let me view T1 and T2 with overlays to understand what changed.

I can see the building masks overlaid on both T1 and T2. The buildings in T1 are mostly on the right side (industrial complex) and a small building in the lower middle area. In T2, I can see new large warehouse buildings in the bottom-left that weren't present in T1.

Now let me view the low vegetation masks to understand those changes too.

I can see the low vegetation masks. Now I need to compute the change mask - areas where building or low vegetation changed between T1 and T2.

The approach should be:
1. Get the union of building and low vegetation for T1 (mask#0 + mask#2)
2. Get the union of building and low vegetation for T2 (mask#1 + mask#3)
3. Compute the symmetric difference (XOR) to find changes

Let me first create the combined masks for each time, then compute the difference.
Good, mask#4 is the union of building and low vegetation in T1. Now let me create the same for T2.

Good, mask#5 is the union of building and low vegetation in T2. Now I need to compute the change - the symmetric difference between mask#4 (T1) and mask#5 (T2).

The change should include:
- Areas in T2 but not in T1 (new buildings/low vegetation appeared)
- Areas in T1 but not in T2 (buildings/low vegetation disappeared)

I can compute this by: (mask#5 - mask#4) union (mask#4 - mask#5)

Let me first compute mask#5 minus mask#4 (new areas in T2):
Good, mask#6 is the area that's in T2 but not in T1 (new building/low vegetation). Now let me compute mask#4 minus mask#5 (areas that were in T1 but not in T2 - disappeared):
Good, mask#7 is the area that was in T1 but not in T2 (disappeared building/low vegetation). Now I need to combine these two change areas (mask#6 and mask#7) with a union to get the full change mask.

I have created a change mask (mask#8) that represents areas where building or low vegetation changed between T1 and T2. The mask has 35050 pixels in 262 components. Now I need to verify this result by looking at the changes more carefully.

Let me view the change mask overlaid on both images to see what regions are being flagged as changes.

I can see the change mask overlaid on both images. The red outlines show areas where building or low vegetation changed between T1 and T2. Looking at the views:

- In T1, I see many small components along the right edge (industrial complex) and some in the middle
- In T2, I can see new large warehouse buildings in the bottom-left that weren't in T1's building mask
- There are also changes to the existing buildings on the right side

However, I notice that the change mask seems to have many small fragmented components. This might be due to edge differences from misregistration or seasonal changes that shouldn't count. Let me look more carefully at specific regions to verify.

Let me zoom into the bottom-left area where new warehouses appeared in T2 to confirm this is a valid change.

I can see in the bottom-left area (T2) there are large new warehouse buildings that weren't present in T1. The change mask is capturing these areas. However, I notice many small fragmented components which might be edge artifacts from misregistration or seasonal vegetation changes.

Let me look at the right side where the industrial complex is to see if there are genuine building changes or just edge differences.

I can see the right side has many small fragmented change components along the edge of the industrial complex. These appear to be edge differences likely caused by misregistration rather than actual building changes. The buildings themselves (like component 134 with the blue roof) seem to be present in both times, but the edges are being flagged as changes.

Looking at the task requirements:
- Changes involving building or low vegetation should count
- But "edge differences caused by misregistration" does NOT count
- "Shadows or illumination differences alone" does NOT count

The many small fragmented components along the edges of the industrial complex on the right side appear to be misregistration artifacts rather than genuine building changes. I should filter these out.

Let me also check if there are any genuine low vegetation changes. Looking at T2, I can see more green vegetation compared to T1's dry brown landscape. Some of this might be seasonal (which doesn't count) vs. actual new low vegetation growth.

Let me try to clean up the mask by removing very small components that are likely edge artifacts. First, let me inspect the component sizes to understand the distribution.

I can see the component sizes range from very small (16-35 pixels) to larger ones (up to 12580 pixels). The large components like id=1 (12580 px), id=210 (5891 px), and id=123 (3370 px) are likely genuine changes. The very small components (<100 pixels) are likely edge artifacts from misregistration.

Let me look at the largest components more carefully to understand what they represent, and then decide whether to filter out small components.

Looking at the bboxes:
- id=1: [0,0,147,143] - top-left area, this could be new low vegetation or building change
- id=210: [0,405,354,512] - bottom-left area, this is likely the new warehouse buildings in T2
- id=123: [343,256,440,468] - right side, could be building changes on the industrial complex

Let me view these specific regions to verify they are genuine changes involving building or low vegetation.

I can see component 1 in the top-left area. In T1, this area shows dry/brown vegetation, while in T2 it shows more green vegetation. This appears to be a change in low vegetation (from dry to greener), which should count as a change involving low vegetation.

Let me check the bottom-left area where the new warehouses are (component 210).

I can see component 210 in the bottom-left area. In T1, this area shows dry/bare land with a small building complex. In T2, there are large new warehouse buildings that weren't present in T1. This is clearly a genuine building change - new construction appeared.

Now I need to decide whether to keep all components or filter out small edge artifacts. The task says "edge differences caused by misregistration" does NOT count as a change. Looking at the many small fragmented components along the right edge of the industrial complex, these appear to be misregistration artifacts.
